recentItems.title: Glimpses along the Way   A Train Journey from Stewarton to Stranraer
recentItems.description: The Girvan to Stranraer line is soon to be a 'one engine in steam' line with a single token issued at Girvan signal box. At present passing loops exist at Girvan, Kilkerran, Barrhill, Glenwhilly and Dunragit, with token exchanges at Glenwhilly and Dunragit. Barrhill is staffed with a signal box and the passing loop is in use. The points at Stranraer have been removed and therefore the second platform cannot be accessed and signalling is redundant.

recentItems.title: Hopton Heath railway station, Heart of Wales Line, Shropshire
recentItems.description: Hopton Heath railway station lies on the Heart of Wales Line that tuns between Llanelli and Craven Arms. It is a request stop and has a single platform, the passing loop and signal box were removed in 1965. The station has 5/6 trains a day in each direction and two each way on Sundays.

recentItems.title: Creating the 'Chapeltoun and Trewithen Railway' in 'T' Gauge
recentItems.description: Creating a 'Set of Memories' using 'T' Gauge track and 1:450 scale buildings, figures, trees, etc. The sites on the railway layout are mostly linked to places in Ayrshire, Nithsdale and a few are elsewhere in the UK. The layout is only 90cms by 30cms and it is transported in a folding case. The locomotives are powered by a controller with three AA batteries. Steam locomotives are not available.

recentItems.title: Balgray Railway Station, Neilston Branch
recentItems.description: Balgray railway station was opened on the Neilston Branch on 27 September 2026 to serve the Barrhead area. The line used to continue through Uplawmoor and Kilwinning to Irvine and Ardrossan. The station to the east is Patterton and Neilston lies to the west. Trains arrive every 30 minutes and run through to Glasgow Central.

recentItems.title: Corsehill Castle and the Origins of the Clan Cunningham
recentItems.description: This video explores the legend of the origins of the ancient Scottish Clan Cunningham and explores the facts and the popular legend of Friskin and King Malcolm Canmore.

recentItems.title: Bedrule Church, Scottish Borders
recentItems.description: Bedrule Church replaced an earlier chapel and was paid for by the Usher family. The church contains part of a Viking hog-back stone and many shields bearing the coats of arms of local families. The Caln Comyn once held these lands and later they passed to the Douglas Clan. The motto of 'I Saved the King' belongs to the Turnbulls, one of whom supposedly saved Robert the Bruce from a wild bull. The church nows belongs to the community.

recentItems.title: Legerwood Kirk, 1127, Scottish Borders
recentItems.description: Legerwood Kirk is one of Scotland's oldest churches and is located near Jedburgh in the Scottish Borders. The Reverend Calderwood was a Covenanter and after losing his church he held illegal conventicles for his parishoners. Grizzel Cochrane is buried here with her husband John Kerr of Morriston. She is remembered for saving her father from execution by taking the death warrant from the courier, dressed as a highywayman.

recentItems.title: St Cattan's Kirk and Mausoleums, Aberuthven, Perth and Kinross
recentItems.description: St Cattan's is one of Scotland's oldest Christian sites. The ruins date from the 13th century and it ceased to be a parish church in  1673. Two of the mausoleums have been built within the old kirk and the old laird's loft was converted in 1736 by John Adam to become the burial site of the Graham's who became the Dukes of Montrose. The parents of the 'Great Montrose,' James Graham are said to be buried here.

recentItems.title: Johnstone Railway Station, Renfrewshire, Ayrshire Coast Line.
recentItems.description: Johnstone railway station was opened in 1840 by the Glasgow, Paisley, Kilmarnock and Ayr Railway. It was known as Johnstone High for a few years. A busy station with regular services. A large goods yard was once located here and one of the sidings served a basin on the Glasgow, Paisley and Ayr Canal. Cars from the Linwood Car Plant were once loaded on to trains nearby.

recentItems.title: The Wester Pickston Railway near Methven in Perth and Kinross
recentItems.description: The Scottish Model Engineering Trust moved here from Perth in 2002 and have built a 2 km long line with 7.25 and 5 inch mixed gauge track. On the two loops are Geoff's Halt, Duck End Station and the main sttaion at Pickston. The line has electric light signalling. Steam and diesel locomotives are in use.

recentItems.title: The Lathalmond Railway Museum, Dunfermline
recentItems.description: The Lathalmond Railway Museum has been built on the site of the old WWII Royal Navy Stores Depot. The standard gauge line is quite short at the moment. A small station has been built and a signal box. The old loco shed is still in use. Hunslet and Andrew Barclay diesel locomotives are in use.

recentItems.title: Milliken Park railway station, Ayrshire Coast Line, Johnstone
recentItems.description:
Milliken Park is a station dating from 1989 that replaced the old station closed in 1966 that lay slightly closer to Johnstone. The next station
towards Ayr is Howwood. Trains call generally every 30 mins. Unusually
no car park is provided, however a large housing estate is close by. The name 'Cochrane Mill' was first used for the 1840 station, however it
became 'Milliken' in 1853 after the businessman who purchased the land.
